paragraphs: This list is for self-questioning only and does not constitute recruitment, capability or performance conclusions. This page is written according to the US O*NET-SOC25-1124.00 for postsecondary foreign language and literature teachers: teaching languages other than English and their literature at the higher education level, including American Sign Language teachers; covering both teaching-focused and teaching-and-research staff. Specific qualifications, appointment and authority are verified by jurisdiction and institution.

Safety exercise | use the complete fictional 16-week beginner Spanish course task below, and verify the same objectives and marking for two parallel classes, the S01 mis-entry correction 78.4 (a difference of 2.25), the S02 total of 72.2 and the S03 absence awaiting verification; complete the course, classroom activities, language questions and rubric, and the anomaly handover. Time limit 90 minutes, do not use real student records, and do not judge similar text from S04 as plagiarism directly.

Fit signals | O*NET points of focus: using email every day (92%), working indoors in an environmentally controlled environment every day (80%), a lot of freedom to determine tasks and priorities (58%), a typical working week of more than 40 hours (74%), decision freedom considerable (53%), public speaking every day (49%), face-to-face discussions with individuals and teams every day (50%), continuous contact with others (42%), sitting more than half the time (43%). If you are willing to invest in specialist language and literature study over the long term and can push teaching, office hours, marking and research writing forward in parallel, the daily requirements of this occupation are closer to your way of working.

Caution signals | O*NET38% answered that competition is extremely high, 44% experience time pressure once a week or more, 36% write letters and memos every week, 34% make decisions every week, 34% have an important impact on unit results, and 35% rated precision fairly important. The typical US qualification for this occupation is a doctorate or professional degree, with some positions accepting a master's degree; this is not extrapolated to a Chinese statutory qualification or to any individual institution's requirements. Long study, public lecturing and continuous writing are work costs that need real experience and weighing.

Taking on the judgement | real fit comes from being able to do three things in the same academic year: teach the course well (course design and lecturing and discussion, setting and marking and feedback, office hours and academic advice), push research and professional development forward (literature and research writing and publication, academic exchange, updating teaching methods), and take on reviewable academic and record responsibility (grades and attendance and teaching files, academic integrity and course committee matters, supervision and references). It is suggested to test this through one verifiable experience (serving as a course teaching assistant and independently teaching several units, completing a course design and marking rubric, or completing a small research and writing project and receiving peer review), rather than relying only on the conclusion of an interest questionnaire.

Safety work sample | the complete prompt below gives 16 weeks, 32 class hours per class, two classes of 24 students each, the 20/20/25/35 weightings and three fictional student records; submit within 90 minutes the objectives and progress, a 40-minute class, the reading response questions and marking answers, the grade trial calculation and the handover awaiting verification. S01 original script 76 mis-entered as 67, S03 absent, and S04 has only a doubt awaiting verification. The course rules are exercise assumptions and cannot be used for real grades.

Occupational scope | teaching language and literature courses in languages other than English at the higher education level, including American Sign Language (ASL) teachers; covering both teaching-focused and teaching-and-research staff. Tasks include course materials, lecturing and discussion, setting and marking assessments, office hours and advising, research publication, student records and departmental committee work; O*NET also lists department head, admissions and registration and study abroad programme tasks. It is distinguished from other subjects, translation and basic education positions by the main work object, and additional administrative duties cannot be excluded wholesale on the basis of the occupational classification; authority over marking review, discipline, enrolment and degrees and professional service is subject to local regulations and institutional appointment.

entries: Course design and materials | syllabus and assignments and handouts | write the syllabus and assignments and handouts, setting content and pace and prerequisites according to the objectives.

Classroom lecturing and discussion | lecturing and seminars and language practice | organise classroom lecturing and discussion and train language expression and writing and cross-cultural understanding.
Assessment and marking | setting questions and marking and feedback | set and organise examinations and assignments and papers, mark to consistent standards and give checkable feedback.

Office hours and academic advice | office hours and course selection and careers advice | arrange fixed office hours, advise students on academic study and course selection and career development and write reference letters.

Research and professional development | literature and research writing | track progress in the field and carry out research, write and publish results and take part in academic exchange and collaboration.

Records and academic affairs | grades and attendance and files | record attendance and grades and teaching files, take part in departmental and academic committee affairs and complete handovers and record keeping.

Work context | the O*NET 25-1124.00 work context shows (the percentages below are respondent distributions, not individual working hours or accident rates): the work is dominated by lesson preparation and lecturing and marking and research writing, mostly indoors in a controlled environment with self-directed scheduling.
Environmental conditions | working indoors in an environmentally controlled environment every day (80%).

Communication | using email every day (92%), face-to-face discussions with individuals and teams every day (50%), public speaking every day (49%).
Contact with others | continuous contact with others (42%), telephone conversations at least once a week but not every day (33%).
Time and autonomy | a lot of freedom to determine tasks and priorities (58%), decision freedom considerable (53%), a typical working week of more than 40 hours (74%).

Sitting and physical | sitting more than half the time (43%), physically moderately close to others (50%).
Collaboration and leadership | working with a team is important (38%), leading or coordinating others is important (30%).
Precision and writing | the share answering that precision is fairly important is 35%, writing letters and memos at least once a week but not every day (36%).

Decisions and impact | making decisions at least once a week but not every day (34%), an important impact on colleagues and unit results (34%), time pressure at least once a week but not every day (44%), job competition extremely high (38%).

Environment and pace | O*NET80% of respondents are indoors in a controlled environment every day, 58% consider task scheduling quite free, 53% have considerable decision freedom, 74% have a typical working week over 40 hours, 44% experience time pressure at least once a week but not every day, 38% regard competition as extremely high, and 43% answered that they sit more than half the time. These are respondent distributions, not individual working hours, and are not enough to call the work physically light or to predict eye and voice health outcomes. Teaching assessment and research scheduling, institution type and position requirements must be verified in practice.

Tools and materials | equipment: computers and teaching platforms (learning management systems) and projection and audio-visual equipment, language laboratory equipment, office and reference management software, and grading and attendance and teaching file systems. Materials: textbooks and handouts and reading materials and audio-visual corpora, question banks and marking rubrics, research methods and reference materials, and student assignments and papers and feedback records. Documents: syllabuses and programme plans, school teaching and assessment and academic integrity rules, and student grade and attendance records (including personal information, which must be used per permissions and the minimum necessary principle). All grade and academic and enrolment judgements are subject to the school rules valid for that term.

Design the course and syllabus → prepare and lecture and discuss → set questions and mark and give feedback → office hours and academic advice → research writing and academic exchange → records and files and departmental affairs

Quality and authority | mark per the course objectives and the school assessment rules and retain materials and grade records; routine marking is a teacher's task. Grade corrections and reviews follow institutional procedures, and major discipline, enrolment and degree matters are decided by the authorised body; authority cannot be inferred from the occupational title. Research materials, citations and authorship must be truthful and verifiable.

Adjacent responsibility boundaries | this page covers O*NET-SOC 25-1124.00; adjacent but different occupations include English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary (teaching English language and literature), Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary, Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary, Teaching Assistants, Postsecondary (providing teaching support and marking), Postsecondary Teachers (the broad group covering all subjects), Postsecondary Education Administrators (responsible for enrolment and academic affairs and admissions), History Teachers, Postsecondary and Communications Teachers, Postsecondary. These occupations differ from this one in subject field and scope of authority; matters involving enrolment and degrees and psychological and legal issues are borne by the corresponding positions.

Escalation and review | for grade disputes, first check the original answers, the common marking standard and the entry records, then follow the school review process; for suspected academic misconduct, preserve the evidence without convicting in advance, and refer major discipline, enrolment and degree or safety crises to the appropriate authorised department. Handling of course and personal information must be verified against local regulations and institutional authorisation.
Design the course → lecture and discuss → set questions and mark → office hours and advising → research and writing → records and departmental affairs

Adjacent subjects | postsecondary English language and literature teachers study and teach English language and literature; the difference is the subject object, and it cannot be concluded from this that native-speaker status is required or that all courses can only be taught in English. This occupation takes languages other than English and their literature as its main object.

Difference from area-ethnic-and-cultural-studies-teachers-postsecondary: the latter take area, ethnic and cultural studies as the disciplinary core, with language ability as one research tool; this occupation takes the language and literature itself as the teaching content, emphasising listening, speaking, reading and writing and training in literary and cultural texts.

Core differences from adjacent occupations | postsecondary English language and literature teachers teach English language and literature; area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers take the relevant groups and cultural issues as the disciplinary object; art, drama and music teachers take the corresponding arts courses as the object. This occupation teaches languages other than English and their literature, including American Sign Language. Teaching assistants may assist with discussion, setting questions and marking, and the specific course and final grade authority is verified against the institutional appointment and cannot be inferred from the occupational title; enrolment, major discipline and professional service are verified separately by jurisdiction and authorisation.

Comparison with postsecondary teaching assistants and postsecondary education administrators: teaching assistants prepare materials, lead discussion, mark and answer questions under the teacher's guidance, and the specific course and marking authority depends on the actual appointment; education administration positions mainly handle enrolment, academic affairs, admissions and funding matters, and whether they also teach must be verified separately through the appointment, since it cannot be inferred from the occupational title that they have absolutely no authority.

Before choosing this occupation, compare: the real tasks (the share of lesson preparation and lecturing and marking and office hours and research and writing), qualification and training paths (master's and doctoral degrees, language proficiency evidence, teaching and research direction), working conditions and assessment (semester milestones and review and promotion cycles, job competition and stability, differences by region and institution type), and growth paths (adjunct teaching, teaching-focused positions, tenure-track assistant professor to professor, or moving into curriculum and academic administration positions). Institutions vary considerably (research universities, teaching-focused institutions, community colleges and language programmes) and this should be verified against actual recruitment and on-site experience.

Responsibility boundaries cannot be inferred from the similarity of job titles: although all are teaching and research positions, school-level foreign language teaching, university teaching of languages other than English, language research, translation and interpreting, and teaching support and academic administration differ in qualifications and authority and outputs. Cross-position work requires relearning the curriculum system and qualification requirements and evaluation standards, and the original position's marking and recognition authority cannot be carried over; matters involving enrolment, findings of academic misconduct, degree conferral and psychological and legal issues must be borne by the corresponding responsible parties.

AI task exposure | digital tools may assist with drafting course materials and handouts, initial screening for language exercises and automatic marking, literature search and review drafts, translation assistance and grammar checking, and teaching data analysis and draft question setting. But determining course objectives and assessment standards, classroom lecturing and discussion and feedback, final grade determination, academic integrity judgements, and the guidance and care of students remain with teachers and authorised bodies; task exposure does not equal job replacement.

Occupational definition | teaching language and literature courses in languages other than English at the higher education level, including American Sign Language (ASL) teachers; covering both teaching-focused and teaching-and-research staff. Tasks include course materials, lecturing and discussion, setting and marking assessments, office hours and advising, research publication, student records and departmental committee work; O*NET also lists department head, admissions and registration and study abroad programme tasks. It is distinguished from other subjects, translation and basic education positions by the main work object, and additional administrative duties cannot be excluded wholesale on the basis of the occupational classification; authority over marking review, discipline, enrolment and degrees and professional service is subject to local regulations and institutional appointment.

Data and system thresholds | before adoption, verify: whether student assignment and grade and attendance data can be traced back to the course and semester and marking basis; the permissions and update and retention periods for student personal information (including identifiable information and learning records); whether tools upload student assignments and writing to external services and use them for training; whether the grade definitions and export formats of different tools and teaching platforms are consistent; and whether offline work with records retained is possible during network or platform failure.

Human control points and manual review | course objectives and content, marking standards and final grades, academic integrity judgements, student guidance and care, and research conclusions and citation integrity must be completed by teachers and authorised bodies; any handout, question, marking result, review or data analysis generated by a tool must be checked by a teacher with a trace left before it is used or counted towards assessment.

Residual responsibility | matters that must not be released automatically: whether the course objectives and assessment standards are reasonable, whether grades reflect real learning outcomes, whether academic misconduct exists, students' guidance and care needs, the truthfulness and completeness of research conclusions and citations, and decisions involving enrolment and degrees and privacy. No tool output equals a teaching conclusion or an authorisation decision.

Failure risk | unreviewed tool outputs may cause errors in course materials and questions, distorted marking and feedback, misjudged or missed academic misconduct, fabricated citations and data, and leakage of student personal information, creating teaching and academic and compliance and privacy risk; using automatic marking results directly as the basis for grades may also damage evaluation fairness and teacher-student trust. Before deployment, make clear who reviews and against what original materials.

Employment evidence boundaries | the employment and wage data of this occupation must be distinguished by definition: the US figures from O*NET and the BLS are estimates under a specific statistical definition and cannot be extrapolated directly to mainland China or other regions; China uses industry category average wages as a background proxy, which does not constitute an occupational wage conclusion. Anything generated should be traceable back to the original inputs and sources, and fluent wording must not be treated as correct evidence.

Practical response | first put digital tools into low-risk steps that can be rolled back and audited (draft handouts and practice questions, literature search and grammar checking, teaching data summarisation), subject to teacher approval and the actual classroom; decide whether to expand the scope of use based on error records and student feedback, and always keep manual confirmation for grading and academic integrity and privacy judgements.

Cross-market definition boundaries | the National Bureau of Statistics urban unit average wage release reviewed here is listed by industry category and does not list this occupation separately; the United States gives OEWS estimates by SOC occupation and industry. The two have different objects and coverage, so industry averages are not spliced or converted into occupational wages, and it is not concluded from a single release that no occupational data exist anywhere in China.

Insufficient evidence: the National Bureau of Statistics release reviewed does not list public occupational wage statistics precisely corresponding to 'postsecondary foreign language and literature teachers'; industry averages, recruitment quotes or third-party estimates are not used as substitutes.

Mainland China wage evidence review points | this page provides only statistical definitions, industry background proxies and a register of visible gaps, and does not provide an estimated wage for this occupation. Before using any figure, first confirm whether its statistical definition (industry category / occupation), statistical period, unit of measurement and covered population are comparable with this occupation.

US wage definition | May 2025 OEWS covers full-time and part-time employees reported by employers and excludes the self-employed; it includes basic wages, production bonuses, commissions and tips and excludes overtime, shift differentials, non-production bonuses and employer benefits. This occupation is reported directly as a survey annual wage and no hourly wage is published, so personal hourly wages cannot be back-calculated using 2080 hours, and the figure does not equal all of an individual's contract and project income.

China wage coverage | the NBS2025 urban unit average wage release reviewed here is listed by industry category, and the education industry figure serves only as background and cannot substitute for this occupation's wage. The survey covers employees of legal entities with 5 or more persons in urban areas and excludes sole proprietors and the self-employed; the income of different teacher contracts or establishment types cannot be inferred from it.

Insufficient evidence: no occupational wage median for postsecondary foreign language and literature teachers that can be verified by occupation was obtained for mainland China; industry category averages are not used as substitutes.

Mainland China wage evidence — statistical period | industry average wages are an annual definition (the figures below are for 2025, published in 2026), which differs from the US May 2025 point-in-time wage on this page, and the two periods cannot be mixed.

Cross-market definition boundaries | mainland China industry average wages and US occupational wages differ in statistical object, period and definition; this page presents them separately with their limitations noted, does not perform currency conversion, and does not treat industry averages as occupational wages.

Unit of measurement | the Chinese education industry annual average wage is pre-tax yuan / year, including bonuses and the personal taxes, social insurance and housing provident fund withheld by the employer; the US occupational wage is US dollars / year. No hourly wage is published for this occupation and the annual wage is calculated directly from the survey. Industry and occupational statistics in the two countries cannot be compared directly.

Insufficient evidence: no postsecondary foreign language and literature teacher wage data verifiable by region or employment form was obtained for mainland China; individual quotes or second-hand accounts are not used as substitutes.

China covered population | NBS employees of legal entities with 5 or more persons in urban areas, split into non-private and private, excluding sole proprietors and the self-employed; the education category includes different positions and is not the wage of postsecondary foreign language and literature teachers.

US wage definition | May 2025 OEWS covers full-time and part-time employees reported by employers and excludes the self-employed; it includes basic wages, production bonuses, commissions and tips and excludes overtime, shift differentials, non-production bonuses and employer benefits. This occupation is reported directly as a survey annual wage and no hourly wage is published, so personal hourly wages cannot be back-calculated using 2080 hours, and the figure does not equal all of an individual's contract and project income.

US wage evidence — statistical period | the wage is May 2025 OEWS; employment, growth and openings are from the 2025—2035 employment projections. The two types of data have different reference points and must not be mixed into a conclusion for the same point in time.

US wage definition | May 2025 OEWS covers full-time and part-time employees reported by employers and excludes the self-employed; it includes basic wages, production bonuses, commissions and tips and excludes overtime, shift differentials, non-production bonuses and employer benefits. This occupation is reported directly as a survey annual wage and no hourly wage is published, so personal hourly wages cannot be back-calculated using 2080 hours, and the figure does not equal all of an individual's contract and project income.

Wage inclusions and exclusions | the pre-tax wages reported by employers include basic wages, production bonuses, commissions and tips; they exclude overtime, shift differentials, non-production bonuses and employer benefits. An individual's total income across contracts or projects cannot be inferred from the occupational distribution.

US wage evidence — occupational scope | the figures on this page correspond to SOC 25-1124 (Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary); they exclude English language and literature teachers, postsecondary (25-1123), area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers (25-1062), art, drama and music teachers (25-1121), the broad postsecondary teachers group (25-1000), teaching assistants (25-9044) and education administrators (11-9033). Wages across occupations must not be mixed.

Statistical limitations | May 2025 OEWS gives 19,830 people employed in this occupation with an employment RSE0.5%; the employment projections programme has a 2025 base period of 24,600 people and about 24,700 in 2035, a listed net increase of about 100 people, growth of 0.2% and 1,600 average annual openings. The programmes and methods differ, and the difference between the two cannot be attributed to part-time work or treated as new positions.

Preface | the following comparison is laid out in four columns: 'occupational direction — core work and outputs — key differences — what it is a better choice for'. Higher education teaching positions are often linked by subject and course, but different subjects do not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, the subject system, course requirements and evaluation standards must be relearned.

Centred on teaching language and literature courses in a language other than English at a higher education institution: designing courses and syllabuses, lecturing and discussion and language and culture training, setting questions and marking and feedback, office hours and academic and careers advice, and research and academic writing and departmental affairs.

Better suited to people willing to invest long term in specialist study of a foreign language and literature, who can balance teaching with research writing, and who are used to lecturing and discussion as the main teaching method.

Output is qualified courses and academic work: syllabuses and teaching materials, grade and feedback records, teaching and academic files, research and publication results, and advising and reference records.
This occupation: postsecondary foreign language and literature teachers

Teaching English language and literature courses, including directions such as linguistics and comparative literature; tasks may include English writing, literary text discussion and research. The subject object differs from this occupation, which does not mean all courses must be taught in English.

Better suited to people investing long term in English language, literature and writing; this occupation focuses on languages other than English and their literature, chosen by subject object, and the language of instruction is not treated as an occupational classification standard.
Output is English courses and English literature research: English writing and literature course materials, grade and feedback records, and research results in English literature and writing.
English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
Centred on area, ethnic and cultural studies: interdisciplinary cultural and social research, ethnic and area and global issues courses, and fieldwork and textual and historical source research.

Better suited to people who take cultural and social studies as the disciplinary core and use language as a research tool; those who prefer teaching the language and literature itself fit this occupation.
Output is cultural studies courses and results: interdisciplinary course materials, area and ethnic research results, and academic publication on social and cultural issues.
Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary

Centred on teaching performance and creation in art, drama and music: directing performance and creation and rehearsal and showcase, evaluating works and performances, and art history and theory courses.
Better suited to people whose teaching focus is performance and creative skill; those who prefer language and text and cross-cultural teaching fit this occupation.
Output is arts teaching and creative performance results: performance and creation courses and rehearsal records, performances and works, and arts teaching and evaluation records.
Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
Centred on history teaching and research: history courses and source reading, historical research and writing, and analysing social change from a historical perspective.

Better suited to people who take history as the disciplinary core and are strong in historical sources and historiography; those who prefer language and literature and cross-cultural texts fit this occupation.
Output is history courses and research results: history course materials, source reading and history papers, and publication in the history direction.
History Teachers, Postsecondary

Centred on supporting teaching and marking and answering questions: leading discussion sections and marking assignments under the teacher's guidance, organising office hours and laboratory or corpus tutorials, and assisting with teaching material preparation.

Better suited to people who take on teaching support and marking within a teaching team while continuing their own study; this occupation carries course design and regular marking, and dispute review authority is verified separately.
Output is teaching support results: discussion section and office hour records, draft marking and grading, and teaching material and corpus preparation records.
Teaching Assistants, Postsecondary

Transition | this page sets adjacent positions side by side by 'which language and subject, and what teaching and evaluation responsibility', to help you judge which kind of higher education teaching and research field you want to invest in long term. Whichever direction you choose, what really determines whether you can take up the work is your disciplinary grounding and language ability, teaching design and interpersonal communication skills, and passing institutional recruitment and teaching demonstration and assessment; an interest questionnaire is only for raising questions.

The O*NET answers on the education needed by newly hired workers are doctorate 73%, master's 18% and bachelor's 9%; these are shares of answers about the education needed, not the education distribution of existing or newly hired workers; the Job Zone is 5 (SVP 8.0 and above). Degree, language, teaching and research results, qualifications and appointment are verified separately; this page has no comparative study of the explanatory power of these factors and does not claim that the degree only affects screening or that outcomes are mainly determined by research results.

Prepare to verify the target position's degree and subject, language and teaching and research evidence, teaching demonstration and evaluation; if the notice requires specific language proficiency evidence, confirm it again, and do not presume a uniform certificate threshold because of non-native status. Positions involving student personal information and research may have additional data and privacy and research ethics training requirements; the specifics are subject to institutional and local rules.
Interests and work context

O*NET interest code SIA (Social—Investigative—Artistic), leaning towards teaching and helping others, researching and analysing humanistic and linguistic phenomena, and language, literature and creative activity. The work context emphasises a lot of freedom to determine tasks and priorities (58%), decision freedom considerable (53%), public speaking every day (49%), face-to-face discussion every day (50%), a typical working week over 40 hours (74%), job competition extremely high (38%), and the share answering that precision is fairly important 35%.
Interest and personality data are for self-questioning only and do not constitute recruitment or performance conclusions.
Equipment and material preparation

Common equipment: computers and teaching platforms (learning management systems) and projection and audio-visual equipment, language laboratory equipment, office and reference management software, and grading and attendance and teaching file systems. Common materials: textbooks and handouts and reading materials and audio-visual corpora, question banks and marking rubrics, research methods and reference materials, and student assignments and papers and feedback records.
Grade and academic and enrolment judgements are subject to the school rules valid for that term.
The complete fictional prompt and simulation rules

Completely fictional prompt | a beginner Spanish reading and writing course, no prerequisites, 16 weeks, 2 × 50 minutes per week per class = 32 class hours; parallel classes A/B with 24 students each. Objective O1: identify the place and time in a campus email; O2: write a short email containing a greeting, request, time and closing. No real school, students, grades or external teaching systems are involved at any point. Common assessment | assignments 20%, speaking 20%, midterm 25%, final 35%, each scored 0—100. Simulation rules: mark an absence as awaiting verification first, and without the course lead's review under the rules do not enter 0 and do not redistribute weightings; both classes use the same marking standard. Teachers may request entry corrections, and formal grades and major course changes must be confirmed per institutional procedure.

Simulation records | S01 assignments 80 and speaking 70 and midterm original script 76 but the table mis-entry as 67 and final 84 and S02=60/90/68/72 and for S03 the scores are 80 and 80 and 80 with the midterm blank and S01 asks for a grade review and another text from S04 is similar to a tool-generated example and there is only a doubt and no confirmed plagiarism finding

Reading material (author's simulation) | Hola, Ana. Nos vemos en la biblioteca el lunes a las diez. ¿Puedes traer el libro? Gracias. Corresponding place biblioteca, weekday lunes, time 10 o'clock. Response question: ask a classmate to borrow a book at the library on Monday at 10 o'clock, and it must have a greeting, request, time and closing; this is a beginner language exercise, not a real email.

Response marking out of 10 | information content 4: place, date, time and borrow request 1 each; language 3: clear meaning, verb form and sentence connection 1 each; politeness 2: greeting and polite request 1 each; conventions 1: closing. Reading 3 points: place / weekday / time 1 each, and the two subtasks are reported separately.

Simulated anomalies and authority | S01 first saves the original script and the old entry and calculates the difference for the course lead; S03 checks the reason for the absence and the applicable procedure; S04 saves the text and the original basis and asks and refers per the school's academic integrity procedure, without convicting on similarity alone. Tools must not read real student information; urgent safety risks are handled per the institution's emergency and professional referral process.

Deliverables | syllabus and objective mapping table, 40-minute activity design, reading and response questions with a common marking sample, weighted grade trial calculation for three people and anomaly table, office hour arrangements, archive retention and permission description, and a one-page handover summary. Mark everything as simulated with a version; do not fabricate classes, reviewers or approval records.

Suggested 90-minute allocation | prompt checking 15, syllabus 15, activity 20, question setting and marking 20, anomalies and records 10, summary 10; this is only a timed sample and does not mean 90 minutes is enough to prepare real semester teaching.
Course, marking and anomaly tasks

Task 1 | divide the 16 weeks into weeks 1—4 basic email, weeks 5—8 time and place and midterm, weeks 9—12 requests and feedback, and weeks 13—16 integrated writing and final; each segment is 8 class hours, 32 in total, both classes have the same progress and marking, and the classroom materials correspond to O1/O2. Task 2 | design a 40-minute unit and reading / response questions; give an actionable marking standard and at least one answer, marking the O1/O2 evidence separately; use the same rubric to trial-mark fictional answers from both classes, record disagreements and do not substitute language fluency for content checking.

Task 3 | check the S01 mis-entry and the two complete grade sets, keep the S03 absence as awaiting verification; write the handling and referral recipients for the S01 review and the S04 doubt; write the weekly office hours, record version and access permissions, and list which facts or approvals are still awaiting confirmation.
Reference answer and trial calculation

Reference answer: course and class | four segments of 8 class hours each, 32 in total. A 40-minute activity could be objective introduction 5, reading the email to find place weekday time 10, group writing of the request 15, peer marking per the rubric 5, and summary feedback 5. An office hour example is 30 minutes every Tuesday, limited to this simulated course's objectives and marking explanation; actual class times are verified separately. Reference answer: language and marking | O1: library, Monday, 10 o'clock, 1 each, 3 in total. O2 may answer Hola, Ana. ¿Puedes prestarme el libro en la biblioteca el lunes a las diez? Gracias. Saludos. Content 4, language 3, politeness 2, conventions 1 = 10/10; other expressions meeting the rubric can also score, and only one wording is not required.

Reference answer: grades | after checking the original script, S01 = 80 × 0.20 + 70 × 0.20 + 76 × 0.25 + 84 × 0.35 = 78.4; with the mis-entered 67 it is 76.15, a difference of 2.25. S02 = 60 × 0.20 + 90 × 0.20 + 68 × 0.25 + 72 × 0.35 = 72.2. S03 is missing the midterm, so no overall grade is given, 0 is not entered and the weightings are not changed; the weighted total of the known items, 60, cannot be written as a formal overall grade.

Reference answer: anomalies and handover | the S01 old table, original script, recalculation and proposed correction coexist and are sent to the course lead for review per procedure, without pretending they are approved; S03 checks the absence and the basis for a resit; S04 registers only the doubt awaiting verification and saves the materials for the designated academic integrity process. The summary lists the common standard for both classes, the three-person trial calculations and items awaiting verification, the office hour arrangements, and the archive version / access roles; simulated codes also do not replace anonymisation compliance for real materials.
Authority and evidence boundaries of the exercise

Boundary | the above courses, rules, materials, personnel, grades and authority are all the author's fictional exercise. They cannot replace institutional assessment rules, academic misconduct findings, enrolment and degree decisions, teacher qualifications or professional psychological or medical services; routine marking and anomaly review follow the actual appointment and school rules. The work only shows the ability to organise objectives, activities, common marking, data checking and handover awaiting verification; it does not constitute evidence of real teaching effect or employment competence, and non-existent student feedback, peer review or approval must not be filled in.

entries.answer: Occupational scope | teaching language and literature courses in languages other than English at the higher education level, including American Sign Language (ASL) teachers; covering both teaching-focused and teaching-and-research staff. Tasks include course materials, lecturing and discussion, setting and marking assessments, office hours and advising, research publication, student records and departmental committee work; O*NET also lists department head, admissions and registration and study abroad programme tasks. It is distinguished from other subjects, translation and basic education positions by the main work object, and additional administrative duties cannot be excluded wholesale on the basis of the occupational classification; authority over marking review, discipline, enrolment and degrees and professional service is subject to local regulations and institutional appointment.
entries.question: What does this occupation actually do?

entries.answer: Postsecondary English language and literature teachers take English language and literature as the subject content, while area, ethnic and cultural studies, art, drama and music, and history teachers each have their own main subject object; classroom language is not the sole classification basis. Teaching assistants may support materials, discussion, setting questions and marking, and the specific teaching and final grade authority is verified against the appointment. This occupation teaches languages other than English and their literature, including American Sign Language, and carries teaching and possibly research tasks.

entries.answer: The O*NET work context shows: using email every day 92%, working indoors in an environmentally controlled environment every day 80%, a lot of freedom to determine tasks and priorities 58%, decision freedom considerable 53%, a typical working week over 40 hours 74%, public speaking every day 49%, face-to-face discussion every day 50%, sitting more than half the time 43%, time pressure once a week or more 44%, and job competition extremely high 38%. Course and review milestones cluster together, and the burden can be managed by arranging semester work and routine sensibly, but public lecturing and continuous writing and assessment pressure are real costs.
entries.question: What are the work pace and pressure like?

entries.answer: The impact is mainly in preparation and search and initial screening steps: drafting course materials and handouts and questions, literature search and review drafts, language exercises and grammar checking, translation assistance, and assignment initial screening and learning analytics can be assisted by tools; course objectives and assessment standards, classroom lecturing and discussion, final grade determination, academic integrity judgements, student guidance and care, and research conclusions and citation completeness remain the responsibility of teachers and authorised bodies. Task exposure does not equal job replacement.

entries.answer: The O*NET answers on the education needed are doctorate 73%, master's 18% and bachelor's 9%, which is not a personnel distribution; US four-year institutions usually require a doctorate and some community colleges and adjunct positions accept a master's degree. Under the Chinese Teachers Law the education condition, qualification recognition and institutional appointment are verified separately and are not interchangeable.

entries.answer: China operates a teacher qualification system in accordance with the law, and education, training, recognition and appointment are not the same thing; the typical US qualification for this occupation and one institution's requirements cannot replace Chinese recognition. Language and research training depend on the specific position, and not all training or a particular language certificate is written up as a generally statutory qualification.

entries.answer: The failure situations summarised by the author include inconsistent grading records, misjudged academic doubts, improper handling of student safety or personal information, and untrue citations and task scheduling conflicts; these do not represent measured incidence rates. Marking is a teacher task, and review, discipline and enrolment and degrees follow the actual school rules and authority. Working hours and sitting posture data do not predict individual illness.
